THE FIRST ADDRESS OF MOSHE — CHAPTERS 1 THROUGH 4

DEVARIM — CHAPTER 1 The Journey Retold

1:1 These are the words which Moshe spoke to all Yisra'el beyond the Yarden; in the wilderness, in the Aravah, over against Suf, between Paran and Tofel, and Lavan, and Chatzerot, and Di-Zahav.

1:2 It is eleven days' journey from Chorev to Kadesh-Barnea by the way of mount Se'ir.

1:3 And it came to pass in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, that Moshe spoke to the children of Yisra'el, according to all that YHWH had given him in commandment to them;

1:4 after he had struck Sichon the king of the Emori, who dwelt in Cheshbon, and Og the king of Bashan, who dwelt in Ashtarot, at Edre'i;

1:5 beyond the Yarden, in the land of Mo'av, Moshe took it upon himself to expound this law, saying:

1:6 YHWH our Creator spoke to us at Chorev, saying: You have dwelt long enough in this mountain;

1:7 turn, and take your journey, and go to the hill country of the Emori and to all the places near it, in the Aravah, in the hill country, and in the lowland, and in the South, and by the sea-shore; the land of the Kena'ani, and the Levanon, as far as the great river, the river Perat.

1:8 Behold, I have set the land before you: go in and possess the land which YHWH swore to your fathers, to Avraham, to Yitzhak, and to Ya'akov, to give to them and to their seed after them.

1:9 And I spoke to you at that time, saying: I am not able to bear you myself alone;

1:10 YHWH your Creator has multiplied you, and behold, you are this day as the stars of heaven for multitude.

1:11 YHWH, the Creator of your fathers, make you a thousand times so many more as you are, and bless you, as he has promised you!

1:12 How can I myself alone bear your trouble, and your burden, and your strife?

1:13 Get for yourselves, from each one of your tribes, wise men, and understanding, and known men, and I will make them heads over you.

1:14 And you answered me, and said: The thing which you have spoken is good for us to do.

1:15 So I took the heads of your tribes, wise men, and known men, and made them heads over you: captains of thousands, and captains of hundreds, and captains of fifties, and captains of tens, and officers, tribe by tribe.

1:16 And I charged your judges at that time, saying: Hear the causes between your brothers, and judge righteously between a man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him.

1:17 You shall not respect persons in judgment; you shall hear the small and the great alike; you shall not be afraid of the face of any man; for the judgment belongs to the Creator; and the cause that is too hard for you, you shall bring to me, and I will hear it.

1:18 And I commanded you at that time all the things which you should do.

1:19 And we journeyed from Chorev, and went through all that great and dreadful wilderness which you saw, by the way to the hill country of the Emori, as YHWH our Creator commanded us; and we came to Kadesh-Barnea.

1:20 And I said to you: You have come to the hill country of the Emori, which YHWH our Creator gives to us.

1:21 Behold, YHWH your Creator has set the land before you: go up, take possession, as YHWH, the Creator of your fathers, has spoken to you; fear not, neither be dismayed.

1:22 And you came near to me, all of you, and said: Let us send men before us, that they may search the land for us, and bring us back word of the way by which we must go up, and the cities to which we shall come.

1:23 And the thing pleased me well; and I took twelve men of you, one man for every tribe;

1:24 and they turned and went up into the mountains, and came to the valley of Eshkol, and spied it out.

1:25 And they took of the fruit of the land in their hands, and brought it down to us, and brought us back word, and said: Good is the land which YHWH our Creator gives to us.

1:26 Yet you would not go up, but rebelled against the commandment of YHWH your Creator;

1:27 and you murmured in your tents, and said: Because YHWH hated us, he has brought us forth out of the land of Mitzrayim, to deliver us into the hand of the Emori, to destroy us.

1:28 Where are we going up? Our brothers have made our heart to melt, saying: The people is greater and taller than we; the cities are great and fortified up to heaven; and moreover we have seen the sons of the Anakim there.

1:29 Then I said to you: Dread not, neither be afraid of them.

1:30 YHWH your Creator who goes before you, he shall fight for you, according to all that he did for you in Mitzrayim before your eyes;

1:31 and in the wilderness, where you have seen how YHWH your Creator bore you, as a man bears his son, in all the way that you went, until you came to this place.

1:32 Yet in this thing you do not believe YHWH your Creator,

1:33 who went before you in the way, to seek you out a place to pitch your tents in: in fire by night, to show you by what way you should go, and in the cloud by day.

1:34 And YHWH heard the voice of your words, and was angry, and swore, saying:

1:35 Surely there shall not one of these men, even this evil generation, see the good land, which I swore to give to your fathers,

1:36 except Kalev the son of Yefunneh, he shall see it; and to him will I give the land that he has trodden upon, and to his children; because he has wholly followed YHWH.

1:37 Also YHWH was angry with me for your sakes, saying: You also shall not go in there;

1:38 Yehoshu'a the son of Nun, who stands before you, he shall go in there; encourage him, for he shall cause Yisra'el to inherit it.

1:39 Moreover your little ones, that you said would be a prey, and your children, that this day have no knowledge of good or evil, they shall go in there, and to them will I give it, and they shall possess it.

1:40 But as for you, turn, and take your journey into the wilderness by the way to the Sea of Reeds.

1:41 Then you answered and said to me: We have sinned against YHWH, we will go up and fight, according to all that YHWH our Creator commanded us. And you girded on every man his weapons of war, and deemed it a light thing to go up into the hill country.

1:42 And YHWH said to me: Say to them: Go not up, neither fight; for I am not among you; lest you be smitten before your enemies.

1:43 So I spoke to you, and you did not listen; but you rebelled against the commandment of YHWH, and were presumptuous, and went up into the hill country.

1:44 And the Emori, that dwell in that hill country, came out against you, and chased you, as bees do, and beat you down in Se'ir, even to Chormah.

1:45 And you returned and wept before YHWH; but YHWH listened not to your voice, nor gave ear to you.

1:46 So you stayed in Kadesh many days, according to the days that you stayed there.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing DSS census produces a confirmed reading specific to this chapter this session. Deuteronomy is among the most heavily attested books at Qumran overall (see Book-Level Critical Apparatus, Section 2), but no verse-level match for this chapter's specific content was confirmed from the secondary citations consulted this session.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Two real, disclosed, and substantial tensions between this chapter's retelling and the base narrative already reconstructed in this project: (1) Verses 9-18's account of appointing judges and officers over the people is framed here as Moshe's own initiative, addressed to the people directly, with no mention of Yitro -- differing from Shemot 18:13-26 (where the plan originates with Yitro's counsel to Moshe) and from Bamidbar 11:16-17, 24-25 (where YHWH institutes seventy elders in direct response to Moshe's complaint of being overburdened, a distinct episode with its own participants and mechanism). This reconstruction presents Devarim 1's account exactly as it is given here, without harmonizing it to either earlier passage or asserting which represents an original account and which a retrospective compression. (2) Verse 37's statement that YHWH was angry with Moshe "for your sakes" (i.e., because of the people's rebellion at the report of the spies) gives a different reason for Moshe's exclusion from the land than Bamidbar 20:12's explicit statement that Moshe and Aharon's own failure to sanctify YHWH at the waters of Merivah was the cause. This reconstruction preserves both statements exactly as each text presents them, without resolving the tension or subordinating one account to the other.

DEVARIM — CHAPTER 2 Se'ir, Mo'av, Ammon — The Defeat of Sichon

2:1 Then we turned, and took our journey into the wilderness by the way to the Sea of Reeds, as YHWH spoke to me; and we went around mount Se'ir many days.

2:2 And YHWH spoke to me, saying:

2:3 You have gone around this mountain long enough; turn northward.

2:4 And command the people, saying: You are to pass through the border of your brothers the children of Esav, that dwell in Se'ir; and they will be afraid of you; take good heed to yourselves therefore;

2:5 contend not with them; for I will not give you of their land, no, not so much as for the sole of the foot to tread on; because I have given mount Se'ir to Esav for a possession.

2:6 You shall purchase food from them for money, that you may eat; and you shall also buy water from them for money, that you may drink.

2:7 For YHWH your Creator has blessed you in all the work of your hand; he has known your walking through this great wilderness; these forty years YHWH your Creator has been with you; you have lacked nothing.

2:8 So we passed by from our brothers the children of Esav, that dwell in Se'ir, from the way of the Aravah, from Eilat and from Etzyon-Gever. And we turned and passed by the way of the wilderness of Mo'av.

2:9 And YHWH said to me: Be not at enmity with Mo'av, neither contend with them in battle; for I will not give you of his land for a possession; because I have given Ar to the children of Lot for a possession.

2:10 The Eimim dwelt therein aforetime, a people great, and many, and tall, as the Anakim;

2:11 these also are accounted Refa'im, as the Anakim; but the Moabites call them Eimim.

2:12 And in Se'ir dwelt the Chorim aforetime, but the children of Esav succeeded them; and they destroyed them from before them, and dwelt in their stead; as Yisra'el did to the land of his possession, which YHWH gave to them.

2:13 Now rise up, and get over the brook Zered. And we went over the brook Zered.

2:14 And the days in which we went from Kadesh-Barnea, until we came over the brook Zered, were thirty-eight years; until all the generation, even the men of war, were consumed from the midst of the camp, as YHWH swore to them.

2:15 Moreover the hand of YHWH was against them, to discomfit them from the midst of the camp, until they were consumed.

2:16 So it came to pass, when all the men of war were consumed and dead from among the people,

2:17 that YHWH spoke to me saying:

2:18 You are this day to pass over the border of Mo'av, even Ar;

2:19 and when you come near over against the children of Ammon, harass them not, nor contend with them; for I will not give you of the land of the children of Ammon for a possession; because I have given it to the children of Lot for a possession.

2:20 That also is accounted a land of Refa'im: Refa'im dwelt therein aforetime; but the Ammonites call them Zamzummim,

2:21 a people great, and many, and tall, as the Anakim; but YHWH destroyed them before them; and they succeeded them, and dwelt in their stead;

2:22 as he did for the children of Esav, that dwell in Se'ir, when he destroyed the Chorim from before them; and they succeeded them, and dwelt in their stead even to this day;

2:23 and the Avim, that dwelt in villages as far as Azzah, the Kaftorim, that came forth out of Kaftor, destroyed them, and dwelt in their stead.

2:24 Rise up, take your journey, and pass over the valley of Arnon; behold, I have given into your hand Sichon the Emori, king of Cheshbon, and his land; begin to possess it, and contend with him in battle.

2:25 This day will I begin to put the dread of you and the fear of you upon the peoples that are under the whole heaven, who, when they hear the report of you, shall tremble, and be in anguish because of you.

2:26 And I sent messengers out of the wilderness of Kedemot to Sichon king of Cheshbon with words of peace, saying:

2:27 Let me pass through your land; I will go along by the highway, I will neither turn to the right hand nor to the left.

2:28 You shall sell me food for money, that I may eat; and give me water for money, that I may drink; only let me pass through on my feet;

2:29 as the children of Esav that dwell in Se'ir, and the Moabites that dwell in Ar, did to me; until I shall pass over the Yarden into the land which YHWH our Creator gives us.

2:30 But Sichon king of Cheshbon would not let us pass by him; for YHWH your Creator hardened his spirit, and made his heart obstinate, that he might deliver him into your hand, as it is this day.

2:31 And YHWH said to me: Behold, I have begun to deliver up Sichon and his land before you; begin to possess it, to possess his land.

2:32 Then Sichon came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Yahatz.

2:33 And YHWH our Creator delivered him up before us; and we struck him, and his sons, and all his people.

2:34 And we took all his cities at that time, and utterly destroyed every city, the men, and the women, and the little ones; we left none remaining;

2:35 only the cattle we took for a prey to ourselves, with the spoil of the cities which we had taken.

2:36 From Aro'er, which is on the edge of the valley of Arnon, and from the city that is in the valley, even to Gil'ad, there was not a city too high for us: YHWH our Creator delivered up all before us.

2:37 Only to the land of the children of Ammon you did not come near: all the side of the river Yabok, and the cities of the hill country, and wherever YHWH our Creator forbade us.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing DSS census produces a confirmed reading specific to this chapter this session. Deuteronomy is among the most heavily attested books at Qumran overall (see Book-Level Critical Apparatus, Section 2), but no verse-level match for this chapter's specific content was confirmed from the secondary citations consulted this session.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] A real, significant, and previously undocumented-in-this-project contradiction: verse 29's claim that "the children of Esav that dwell in Se'ir... did to me" (i.e., granted Yisra'el passage on payment, matching the terms requested of Sichon in vv.27-28) directly conflicts with Bamidbar 20:18-21 (already reconstructed in this project), where Edom explicitly refuses passage ("Edom said to him: You shall not pass through me, lest I come out with the sword against you"; "Edom refused to give Yisra'el passage through his border"). This reconstruction preserves both statements exactly as each text presents them, without harmonizing v.29's claim to Bamidbar's account or subordinating either text to the other; this is disclosed here as a genuine, substantial textual tension between the base narrative and Devarim's retrospective framing, of the kind widely discussed in source-critical scholarship on Deuteronomy's relationship to the Torah's other books. Verse 30's statement that YHWH "hardened his spirit, and made his heart obstinate" so that Sichon would refuse passage is preserved as MT presents it, structurally parallel to but independent of the hardening language already reconstructed in Shemot's plague narrative, without importing that earlier discussion here.

DEVARIM — CHAPTER 3 The Defeat of Og — Moshe's Plea Denied

3:1 Then we turned, and went up the way to Bashan; and Og the king of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Edre'i.

3:2 And YHWH said to me: Fear him not; for I have delivered him, and all his people, and his land, into your hand; and you shall do to him as you did to Sichon king of the Emori, who dwelt at Cheshbon.

3:3 So YHWH our Creator delivered into our hand Og also, the king of Bashan, and all his people; and we struck him until none was left to him remaining.

3:4 And we took all his cities at that time; there was not a city which we did not take from them; sixty cities, all the region of Argov, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

3:5 All these were fortified cities, with high walls, gates, and bars; besides the unwalled towns a great many.

3:6 And we utterly destroyed them, as we did to Sichon king of Cheshbon, utterly destroying every city, the men, and the women, and the little ones.

3:7 But all the cattle, and the spoil of the cities, we took for a prey to ourselves.

3:8 And we took the land at that time out of the hand of the two kings of the Emori, that were beyond the Yarden, from the valley of Arnon to mount Chermon --

3:9 which Chermon the Tzidonim call Sirion, and the Emori call it Senir --

3:10 all the cities of the plain, and all Gil'ad, and all Bashan, to Salkhah, and Edre'i, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

3:11 For only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of the Refa'im; behold, his bedstead was a bedstead of iron; is it not in Rabbah of the children of Ammon? Nine cubits was its length, and four cubits its breadth, after the cubit of a man.

3:12 And this land we took in possession at that time; from Aro'er, which is by the valley of Arnon, and half the hill country of Gil'ad, and its cities, I gave to the Re'uvenites and to the Gadites;

3:13 and the rest of Gil'ad, and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to the half-tribe of Menasheh: all the region of Argov -- all that Bashan is called the land of Refa'im.

3:14 Ya'ir the son of Menasheh took all the region of Argov, to the border of the Geshurites and the Ma'akhatites, and called them, even Bashan, after his own name, Chavot-Ya'ir, to this day.

3:15 And to Machir I gave Gil'ad.

3:16 And to the Re'uvenites and to the Gadites I gave from Gil'ad even to the valley of Arnon, the middle of the valley for a border, even to the river Yabok, which is the border of the children of Ammon;

3:17 the Aravah also, the Yarden being its border, from Kinneret even to the sea of the Aravah, the Salt Sea, under the slopes of Pisgah eastward.

3:18 And I commanded you at that time, saying: YHWH your Creator has given you this land to possess it; you shall pass over armed before your brothers the children of Yisra'el, all the men of valor.

3:19 But your wives, and your little ones, and your cattle -- I know that you have much cattle -- shall stay in your cities which I have given you;

3:20 until YHWH give rest to your brothers, as to you, and they also possess the land which YHWH your Creator gives them beyond the Yarden; then shall you return every man to his possession, which I have given you.

3:21 And I commanded Yehoshu'a at that time, saying: Your eyes have seen all that YHWH your Creator has done to these two kings; so shall YHWH do to all the kingdoms where you go over.

3:22 You shall not fear them; for YHWH your Creator, he it is that fights for you.

3:23 And I pleaded with YHWH at that time, saying:

3:24 My Creator, YHWH, you have begun to show your servant your greatness, and your strong hand; for what god is there in heaven or on earth, that can do according to your works, and according to your mighty acts?

3:25 Let me go over, I pray you, and see the good land that is beyond the Yarden, that goodly hill country, and the Levanon.

3:26 But YHWH was angry with me for your sakes, and listened not to me; and YHWH said to me: Let it suffice you; speak no more to me of this matter.

3:27 Go up to the top of Pisgah, and lift up your eyes westward, and northward, and southward, and eastward, and behold with your eyes; for you shall not go over this Yarden.

3:28 But charge Yehoshu'a, and encourage him, and strengthen him; for he shall go over before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land which you shall see.

3:29 So we stayed in the valley over against Beit-Pe'or.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing DSS census produces a confirmed reading specific to this chapter this session. Deuteronomy is among the most heavily attested books at Qumran overall (see Book-Level Critical Apparatus, Section 2), but no verse-level match for this chapter's specific content was confirmed from the secondary citations consulted this session.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verse 11's claim that Og's iron bedstead was preserved and could be seen "in Rabbah of the children of Ammon," with specific stated dimensions, is a real, disclosed claim embedded in the text itself, presenting a physical artifact as verifiable at a named location; this reconstruction renders the claim exactly as MT states it. Classification: UNVERIFIED-OPEN -- no archaeological confirmation of such an artifact exists, and this reconstruction neither asserts nor denies its historicity, presenting only what the text itself claims. Verses 24 and 26's rare double divine-address אדני יהוה is rendered "My Creator, YHWH," preserving the double-invocation structure of the Hebrew without using "Lord," consistent with the Divine Name Policy. Verses 23-28's account of Moshe's plea and its denial is rendered without cross-referencing or attempting to reconcile it with the differing stated reasons for Moshe's exclusion already disclosed at 1:37 and at Bamidbar 20:12 (reconstructed earlier in this project); this chapter's own account (YHWH's anger "for your sakes," v.26) is presented as this chapter itself states it.

DEVARIM — CHAPTER 4 No Form Was Seen — The Cities of Refuge East of the Yarden

4:1 And now, O Yisra'el, listen to the statutes and to the ordinances, which I teach you, to do them; that you may live, and go in and possess the land which YHWH, the Creator of your fathers, gives you.

4:2 You shall not add to the word which I command you, neither shall you diminish from it, that you may keep the commandments of YHWH your Creator which I command you.

4:3 Your eyes have seen what YHWH did at Ba'al-Pe'or; for all the men that followed the Ba'al of Pe'or, YHWH your Creator has destroyed them from your midst.

4:4 But you that did cleave to YHWH your Creator are alive every one of you this day.

4:5 Behold, I have taught you statutes and ordinances, even as YHWH my Creator commanded me, that you should do so in the midst of the land where you go in to possess it.

4:6 Observe therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the peoples, that, when they hear all these statutes, shall say: Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.

4:7 For what great nation is there, that has a god so near to it, as YHWH our Creator is whenever we call upon him?

4:8 And what great nation is there, that has statutes and ordinances so righteous as all this law, which I set before you this day?

4:9 Only take heed to yourself, and keep your soul diligently, lest you forget the things which your eyes saw, and lest they depart from your heart all the days of your life; but make them known to your children and your children's children;

4:10 the day that you stood before YHWH your Creator at Chorev, when YHWH said to me: Assemble the people to me, and I will make them hear my words that they may learn to fear me all the days that they live upon the earth, and that they may teach their children.

4:11 And you came near and stood under the mountain; and the mountain burned with fire to the heart of heaven, with darkness, cloud, and thick darkness.

4:12 And YHWH spoke to you out of the midst of the fire: you heard the voice of words, but you saw no form; only a voice.

4:13 And he declared to you his covenant, which he commanded you to perform, even the ten words; and he wrote them upon two tables of stone.

4:14 And YHWH commanded me at that time to teach you statutes and ordinances, that you might do them in the land where you go over to possess it.

4:15 Take good heed to yourselves therefore -- for you saw no manner of form on the day that YHWH spoke to you at Chorev out of the midst of the fire --

4:16 lest you deal corruptly, and make for yourselves a graven image, even the form of any figure, the likeness of male or female,

4:17 the likeness of any beast that is on the earth, the likeness of any winged fowl that flies in the heaven,

4:18 the likeness of anything that creeps on the ground, the likeness of any fish that is in the water under the earth;

4:19 and lest you lift up your eyes to heaven, and when you see the sun and the moon and the stars, even all the host of heaven, you be drawn away and worship them, and serve them, which YHWH your Creator has allotted to all the peoples under the whole heaven.

4:20 But you has YHWH taken and brought forth out of the iron furnace, out of Mitzrayim, to be to him a people of inheritance, as you are this day.

4:21 And YHWH was angered with me for your sakes, and swore that I should not go over the Yarden, and that I should not go in to that good land, which YHWH your Creator gives you for an inheritance;

4:22 but I must die in this land, I must not go over the Yarden; but you are to go over, and possess that good land.

4:23 Take heed to yourselves, lest you forget the covenant of YHWH your Creator, which he made with you, and make for yourselves a graven image, even the likeness of anything which YHWH your Creator has forbidden you.

4:24 For YHWH your Creator is a devouring fire, a jealous Creator.

4:25 When you shall beget children, and children's children, and you shall have been long in the land, and shall deal corruptly, and make a graven image, even the form of anything, and shall do that which is evil in the sight of YHWH your Creator, to provoke him;

4:26 I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day, that you shall soon utterly perish from off the land whereunto you go over the Yarden to possess it: you shall not prolong your days upon it, but shall utterly be destroyed.

4:27 And YHWH shall scatter you among the peoples, and you shall be left few in number among the nations, whither YHWH shall lead you away.

4:28 And there you shall serve gods, the work of men's hands, wood and stone, which neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.

4:29 But from there you will seek YHWH your Creator; and you shall find him, if you search after him with all your heart and with all your soul.

4:30 In your distress, when all these things have come upon you, in the end of days, you will return to YHWH your Creator, and listen to his voice;

4:31 for YHWH your Creator is a compassionate Creator; he will not fail you, neither destroy you, nor forget the covenant of your fathers which he swore to them.

4:32 For ask now of the days past, which were before you, since the day that the Creator created man upon the earth, and from the one end of heaven to the other, whether there has been any such thing as this great thing is, or has been heard like it?

4:33 Did ever a people hear the voice of the Creator speaking out of the midst of the fire, as you have heard, and live?

4:34 Or has the Creator attempted to go and take for himself a nation from the midst of another nation, by trials, by signs, and by wonders, and by war, and by a mighty hand, and by an outstretched arm, and by great terrors, according to all that YHWH your Creator did for you in Mitzrayim before your eyes?

4:35 To you it was shown, that you might know that YHWH, he is the Creator; there is none else beside him.

4:36 Out of heaven he made you to hear his voice, that he might instruct you; and upon earth he made you to see his great fire; and you heard his words out of the midst of the fire.

4:37 And because he loved your fathers, and chose their seed after them, and brought you out with his presence, with his great power, out of Mitzrayim,

4:38 to drive out nations from before you greater and mightier than you, to bring you in, to give you their land for an inheritance, as it is this day;

4:39 know this day, and lay it to your heart, that YHWH, he is the Creator in heaven above and upon the earth beneath; there is none else.

4:40 And you shall keep his statutes, and his commandments, which I command you this day, that it may go well with you, and with your children after you, and that you may prolong your days upon the land, which YHWH your Creator gives you, for ever.

4:41 Then Moshe separated three cities beyond the Yarden toward the sunrising;

4:42 that the manslayer might flee there, that kills his neighbor unawares, and hated him not in time past; and that fleeing to one of these cities he might live:

[DSS] A major, book-level-significant finding, directly relevant to this chapter: 4QDeut-n (4Q41, the "All Souls Deuteronomy"), already registered in the Book-Level Critical Apparatus, preserves this chapter (5:1-6:1) together with 8:5-10, in that unusual order -- not the canonical sequence -- on a single small manuscript. VERIFIED via convergent secondary academic sourcing (Sidnie White Crawford's published analysis, generally accepted in the field): this ordering, combined with the manuscript's small physical dimensions, indicates it was very probably not a running biblical scroll but a purpose-made excerpt manuscript for personal or liturgical use, not evidence of a variant book-order in a complete Deuteronomy scroll. Separately and significantly: 4QDeut-n's text of the sabbath commandment (vv.12-15 here) is reported to harmonize uniquely, importing the six-day-creation rationale for sabbath observance from the Shemot Decalogue (already reconstructed in this project at Shemot 20:11) into this chapter's own stated rationale (the Exodus from Mitzrayim, vv.14-15) -- a real, disclosed scribal harmonization attempt at Qumran, not adopted into this reconstruction's own translation, which renders this chapter's rationale exactly as MT states it. The primary edition (Crawford; Cross's original catalogue publication) was not independently consulted this session.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The ACR follows its own locked editorial and versification standard, controlled by the project's Hebrew base (MT/UXLC); external editions -- including Mechon-Mamre's Hebrew-English parallel edition, consulted throughout this project for verification and comparison -- are research witnesses and do not themselves define the ACR standard. Devarim chapter 5 is a recognized versification exception, disclosed here for reader orientation: the Decalogue passages (present only at Shemot 20 and here) carry two parallel cantillation traditions within the Masoretic text itself -- the ta'am tachton ("lower" cantillation, used for private study, dividing the passage into fewer, longer verses) and the ta'am elyon ("upper" cantillation, used for public Torah reading, dividing it into more, shorter verses). This project's numbering for this chapter, consistent with the ta'am tachton pattern, ends at verse 29; many English editions (consistent with the ta'am elyon pattern) number the same textual content through verse 33. No textual content is missing under either numbering; this is a versification difference only, not a manuscript variant and not a reconstruction defect.

[CRITICAL NOTE] This chapter's Decalogue differs from the version already reconstructed at Shemot 20:2-14 in several real, disclosed, and substantial particulars, none harmonized here: (1) the sabbath commandment's opening verb is שמור ("observe/guard," v.12) here against זכור ("remember") at Shemot 20:8; (2) the sabbath commandment's stated rationale is the Exodus from Mitzrayim (vv.14-15) here, against the six-day creation and divine rest at Shemot 20:11; (3) verse 14 here explicitly adds that the manservant and maidservant's rest is so that they "may rest as well as you," an emphasis not present in the Shemot 20 sabbath commandment; (4) verse 17's coveting commandment orders "your neighbor's wife" before "your neighbor's house," reversing Shemot 20:14's order (house named before wife), and uses two distinct verbs (חמד for the wife, תתאוה for the house and remaining property) rather than a single repeated verb. This reconstruction presents this chapter's wording exactly as MT gives it, without conforming it to the earlier Shemot text or resolving which, if either, represents a more original wording.

DEVARIM — CHAPTER 15 The Sabbatical Release — Freeing the Hebrew Servant

15:1 At the end of every seven years you shall make a release.

15:2 And this is the manner of the release: every creditor shall release that which he has lent to his neighbor; he shall not exact it of his neighbor and his brother; because YHWH's release has been proclaimed.

15:3 Of a foreigner you may exact it; but whatever of yours is with your brother your hand shall release.

15:4 Howbeit there shall be no needy among you -- for YHWH will surely bless you in the land which YHWH your Creator gives you for an inheritance to possess it --

15:5 if only you diligently listen to the voice of YHWH your Creator, to observe to do all this commandment which I command you this day.

15:6 For YHWH your Creator will bless you, as he promised you; and you shall lend to many nations, but you shall not borrow; and you shall rule over many nations, but they shall not rule over you.

15:7 If there be among you a needy man, one of your brothers, within any of your gates, in your land which YHWH your Creator gives you, you shall not harden your heart, nor shut your hand from your needy brother;

15:8 but you shall surely open your hand to him, and shall surely lend him sufficient for his need in that which he wants.

15:9 Beware that there be not a base thought in your heart, saying: The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand; and your eye be evil against your needy brother, and you give him nothing; and he cry to YHWH against you, and it be sin in you.

15:10 You shall surely give him, and your heart shall not be grieved when you give to him; because for this thing YHWH your Creator will bless you in all your work, and in all that you put your hand to.

15:11 For the poor shall never cease out of the land; therefore I command you, saying: You shall surely open your hand to your poor and needy brother, in your land.

15:12 If your brother, a Hebrew man, or a Hebrew woman, be sold to you, he shall serve you six years; and in the seventh year you shall let him go free from you.

15:13 And when you let him go free from you, you shall not let him go empty;

15:14 you shall furnish him liberally out of your flock, and out of your threshing floor, and out of your winepress: of that with which YHWH your Creator has blessed you, you shall give to him.

15:15 And you shall remember that you were a bondman in the land of Mitzrayim, and YHWH your Creator redeemed you; therefore I command you this thing today.

15:16 And it shall be, if he say to you: I will not go out from you; because he loves you and your house, because he fares well with you;

15:17 then you shall take an awl, and thrust it through his ear and into the door, and he shall be your bondman for ever. And also to your bondwoman you shall do likewise.

15:18 It shall not seem hard to you, when you let him go free from you; for to the double of the hire of a hired servant has he served you six years; and YHWH your Creator will bless you in all that you do.

15:19 All the firstling males that are born of your herd and of your flock you shall sanctify to YHWH your Creator; you shall do no work with the firstling of your ox, nor shear the firstling of your flock.

15:20 You shall eat it before YHWH your Creator year by year in the place which YHWH shall choose, you and your household.

15:21 And if there be any blemish therein, lameness, or blindness, any bad blemish whatsoever, you shall not sacrifice it to YHWH your Creator.

15:22 You shall eat it within your gates; the unclean and the clean may eat it alike, as the gazelle, and as the hart.

15:23 Only you shall not eat its blood; you shall pour it out upon the ground as water.

DEVARIM — CHAPTER 16 The Three Pilgrim Festivals — Justice, Justice

16:1 Observe the month of Aviv, and keep the Pesach to YHWH your Creator; for in the month of Aviv YHWH your Creator brought you forth out of Mitzrayim by night.

16:2 And you shall sacrifice the Pesach offering to YHWH your Creator, of the flock and the herd, in the place which YHWH shall choose to cause his name to dwell there.

16:3 You shall eat no leavened bread with it; seven days shall you eat unleavened bread with it, even the bread of affliction; for in haste did you come forth out of the land of Mitzrayim; that you may remember the day when you came forth out of the land of Mitzrayim all the days of your life.

16:4 And there shall be no leaven seen with you in all your borders seven days; neither shall any of the flesh, which you sacrifice the first day at evening, remain all night until the morning.

16:5 You may not sacrifice the Pesach offering within any of your gates, which YHWH your Creator gives you;

16:6 but at the place which YHWH your Creator shall choose to cause his name to dwell in, there shall you sacrifice the Pesach offering at evening, at the going down of the sun, at the season that you came forth out of Mitzrayim.

16:7 And you shall roast and eat it in the place which YHWH your Creator shall choose; and you shall turn in the morning, and go to your tents.

16:8 Six days shall you eat unleavened bread; and on the seventh day shall be a solemn assembly to YHWH your Creator: you shall do no work therein.

16:9 Seven weeks shall you number for yourself: from the time the sickle is first put to the standing grain shall you begin to number seven weeks.

16:10 And you shall keep the feast of weeks to YHWH your Creator after the measure of the freewill offering of your hand, which you shall give, according as YHWH your Creator blesses you.

16:11 And you shall rejoice before YHWH your Creator, you, and your son, and your daughter, and your man-servant, and your maid-servant, and the Levite that is within your gates, and the stranger, and the fatherless, and the widow, that are in your midst, in the place which YHWH your Creator shall choose to cause his name to dwell there.

16:12 And you shall remember that you were a bondman in Mitzrayim; and you shall observe and do these statutes.

16:13 You shall keep the feast of Sukkot seven days, after you have gathered in from your threshing floor and from your winepress.

16:14 And you shall rejoice in your feast, you, and your son, and your daughter, and your man-servant, and your maid-servant, and the Levite, and the stranger, and the fatherless, and the widow, that are within your gates.

16:15 Seven days shall you keep a feast to YHWH your Creator in the place which YHWH shall choose; because YHWH your Creator shall bless you in all your increase, and in all the work of your hands, and you shall be altogether joyful.

16:16 Three times in a year shall all your males appear before YHWH your Creator in the place which he shall choose: on the feast of unleavened bread, and on the feast of weeks, and on the feast of Sukkot; and they shall not appear before YHWH empty;

16:17 every man shall give as he is able, according to the blessing of YHWH your Creator which he has given you.

16:18 Judges and officers shall you make for yourself in all your gates, which YHWH your Creator gives you, tribe by tribe; and they shall judge the people with righteous judgment.

16:19 You shall not wrest judgment; you shall not respect persons; neither shall you take a bribe; for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise, and perverts the words of the righteous.

16:20 Justice, justice shall you pursue, that you may live, and inherit the land which YHWH your Creator gives you.

16:21 You shall not plant for yourself an Asherah of any kind of tree beside the altar of YHWH your Creator, which you shall make for yourself.

16:22 Neither shall you set up for yourself a pillar, which YHWH your Creator hates.

DEVARIM — CHAPTER 17 Testimony of Witnesses — The Law of the King

17:1 You shall not sacrifice to YHWH your Creator an ox, or a sheep, wherein is a blemish, even any evil thing; for that is an abomination to YHWH your Creator.

17:2 If there be found in your midst, within any of your gates which YHWH your Creator gives you, man or woman, that does that which is evil in the sight of YHWH your Creator, in transgressing his covenant,

17:3 and has gone and served other gods, and worshiped them, or the sun, or the moon, or any of the host of heaven, which I have not commanded;

17:4 and it be told you, and you hear it, then shall you inquire diligently, and behold, if it be true, and the thing certain, that such abomination is done in Yisra'el;

17:5 then shall you bring forth that man or that woman, who have done this evil thing, to your gates, even the man or the woman; and you shall stone them with stones, that they die.

17:6 At the mouth of two witnesses, or three witnesses, shall he that is to die be put to death; at the mouth of one witness he shall not be put to death.

17:7 The hand of the witnesses shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterward the hand of all the people. So shall you put away the evil from your midst.

17:8 If there arise a matter too hard for you in judgment, between blood and blood, between plea and plea, and between stroke and stroke, even matters of controversy within your gates; then shall you arise, and go up to the place which YHWH your Creator shall choose.

17:9 And you shall come to the priests the Levites, and to the judge that shall be in those days; and you shall inquire; and they shall declare to you the sentence of judgment.

17:10 And you shall do according to the tenor of the sentence, which they shall declare to you from that place which YHWH shall choose; and you shall observe to do according to all that they shall teach you.

17:11 According to the law which they shall teach you, and according to the judgment which they shall tell you, shall you do; you shall not turn aside from the sentence which they shall declare to you, to the right hand, nor to the left.

17:12 And the man that does presumptuously, in not listening to the priest that stands to minister there before YHWH your Creator, or to the judge, even that man shall die; and you shall exterminate the evil from Yisra'el.

17:13 And all the people shall hear, and fear, and do no more presumptuously.

17:14 When you have come to the land which YHWH your Creator gives you, and shall possess it, and shall dwell therein; and shall say: I will set a king over me, like all the nations that are round about me;

17:15 you shall in any wise set him king over you, whom YHWH your Creator shall choose: one from among your brothers shall you set king over you; you may not put a foreigner over you, who is not your brother.

17:16 Only he shall not multiply horses to himself, nor cause the people to return to Mitzrayim, to the end that he should multiply horses; forasmuch as YHWH has said to you: You shall henceforth return no more that way.

17:17 Neither shall he multiply wives to himself, that his heart turn not away; neither shall he greatly multiply to himself silver and gold.

17:18 And it shall be, when he sits upon the throne of his kingdom, that he shall write for himself a copy of this law in a book, out of that which is before the priests the Levites.

17:19 And it shall be with him, and he shall read therein all the days of his life; that he may learn to fear YHWH his Creator, to keep all the words of this law and these statutes, to do them;

17:20 that his heart be not lifted up above his brothers, and that he turn not aside from the commandment, to the right hand, or to the left; to the end that he may prolong his days in his kingdom, he and his children, in the midst of Yisra'el.
